The cause is `client/layouts.js:790` — `s.title.length > 30 ? s.title.slice(0, 29) + '…'` — a hard character cap applied in JavaScript before the DOM sees it, which is why `scrollWidth > clientWidth` (the phone audit's only clip test) can never fire on it and why the machine has reported PASS over a truncation two earlier graders pointed at by eye. THE SPACE & LEGIBILITY LAW forbids ellipsis on a name outright, and a fixed cap makes ladder rung 1 structurally impossible. (3) The DARK theme's fill axis is DEAD at 5/10 — `Controls.png` (dark/outlined) and `Controls_dark_full.png` (dark/filled) are BYTE-IDENTICAL over the entire control surface (max per-channel diff 0 across both D-pad columns, the Layout button and the Hide button; the Click button is the same 6039 pixels of rgb(18,26,45) in both), so the desktop Appearance card's promise 'Filled paints the buttons in' does nothing on the default theme. The CSS is innocent — a cascade probe shows body[data-fill="full"] correctly resolves .ctl to rgb(30,41,59) on dark — and a live-page probe caught the cause: `body.dataset.fill` flips back to 'transparent' within half a second of applyUi, because `client/connection.js:78` calls `applyUi(msg.ui || null)` on every `config` frame and `applyUi` falls back to UI_DEFAULT (dark/transparent) for any missing field. The audit never asserts that the look it asked for is still on screen when it shoots — and the SAME cause produces a SECOND wrong picture, which I found by sweeping the page colour of all twelve look shots: `Controls_light_transparent_landscape.png` renders on a DARK page (15,23,42) where its portrait twin renders light (236,238,246).
